title: WAMs and VLAs for Robot Learning | Cosmos Labs
summary: NVIDIA’s Cosmos Labs livestream lays out how World Action Models and vision-language-action models play different roles in robot foundation models, with WAMs modeling future observations and actions while VLAs connect perception, language, and control. It centers on Cosmos 3, which treats action as a native modality alongside video, and shows how Cosmos3-Nano-Policy-DROID can imagine future observations while generating robot actions. The session is framed as a practical path for adapting and deploying these models with open Cosmos models, datasets, recipes, evaluation workflows, and serving resources.

extra.full_text: Building capable robot foundation models requires more than one approach. Vision-language-action (VLA) models and World Action Models (WAMs) - each offer different strengths for robot learning, planning, and control. In this livestream, NVIDIA researchers Danfei Xu US Moritz Benno Reuss CH Thomas Tian US will explore what World Action Models work, how they compare with modern Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models, and why many next-generation robot foundation models combine both approaches. You'll also see how NVIDIA Cosmos 3 treats action as a native modality, enabling robots to predict future observations while generating actions. We'll walk through how Cosmos 3 provides an open workflow for post-training, evaluation, and deployment using open models, datasets, recipes, and serving resources. Whether you're building manipulation policies, training robot foundation models, or exploring embodied AI, this livestream provides a practical understanding of where World Action Models fit into the future of robotics. What You'll Learn: - What World Action Models are and how they differ from and complement Vision-Language-Action models - The strengths, limitations, and tradeoffs of WAMs, VLAs, and emerging hybrid approaches - How Cosmos3-Nano-Policy-DROID imagines future observations while generating robot actions - How NVIDIA Cosmos 3 represents action as a native modality alongside video - How to evaluate, post-train, and adapt Cosmos 3 using open models, datasets, recipes, and serving resources Have questions about how to post-train and deploy NVIDIA Cosmos 3? Drop them live — the NVIDIA team will answer them in real time. summary: KOTRA’s Zurich office says Switzerland’s industrial robot market is shifting from standalone robot sales toward integrated intelligent automation built around AI, machine vision, collaborative robots, and process software. In high-value sectors like pharma, biotech, medical devices, and precision machinery, competitiveness depends less on the robot hardware itself than on process optimization and system integration, so Korean firms are being advised to enter through project-based partnerships with local SI companies and specialized solutions.

title: ‘LG 홈봇 AI 오브제컬렉션 로니(RONi)’ 이색 팝업 체험존 운영
summary: LG is running a pop-up experience zone at Hyundai Department Store Pangyo through August 12 for its new LG HomeBot AI Objet Collection RONi cleaning robot. title: 프리뉴, 카자흐스탄 생산공장 KKDS 개소…중앙亞 드론 시장 진출 ‘날개’
summary: Preneu has opened a Kazakhstan production plant for KKDS, its joint venture with DQB Group’s UMR, and begun local manufacturing aimed at the Central Asian drone market. The move turns a collaboration that began at the 2024 Songdo drone expo into an on-the-ground manufacturing base, giving the Korean UAV designer-manufacturer a regional foothold rather than just an export channel.
